why: A moved every OpenAI/Anthropic-served call including the ChatOpenRouter inner client (which B's own validator flagged as unwrapped), verified it with 116 live Router requests, and then did real system work: four built-and-tested branches whose headline wins — a prompt_cache_key on the already-cache-shaped chat prefix (-73% input per turn) and cheap-model background summarization (48x on compaction) — are exactly the levers an expert would pull for a notes app with a huge stable system prefix and bulk summarization. B shipped only the move plus one policy line, and that line is its central judgment call and is wrong on A's measurements: pinning service_tier "default" doubles cost for no median latency gain, while B's one real improvement (feature labels) stays proposed and several of its call-site readings are mislabelled (chainUtils condensation described as "inline-edit" note rewriting).
A_best: The improvement set is both correct and well-ranked for THIS app: it identifies that the plugin had no cache key despite a caching-shaped prompt layout, proves the key (not the provider) does the work with a controlled no-key arm, and scopes keys only where a prefix actually repeats — skipping prompts under the ~1k cache minimum rather than sprinkling keys everywhere.
B_best: Honest, app-aware reasoning on what should NOT move: Ollama/LM Studio as the privacy feature, Copilot Plus and OpenRouter as gateways in their own right, Perplexity as an index rather than a model, and a principled rejection of cross-vendor fallbacks for a note-taking answer.
A_worst: The aux-model swap makes the app behave differently with and without the Router key — a user who chose Opus silently gets Haiku writing summaries back into their notes and memory file — which strains the "behaviour intact" bar more than the report's disclosure admits, and the validator still showed tests mid-run rather than green.
B_worst: Its one system-level decision is a measured-wrong latency defence: it pays double on every Flex-eligible OpenAI call on the strength of a single 61s gpt-5-nano outlier, applies it blanket while admitting the background calls don't need it, and leaves the app's biggest actual win — prompt caching on the long fixed system prompt — unmeasured and unbuilt.
